_comment: Curated A17 reference material: circuit descriptions from §2-70…§2-79, the
3600-series diagnostic fault codes from §5-2, and the places where the manuals
A17 has no numbered troubleshooting section -- Chapter 5's component-level
procedures run 5-4 through 5-23 and stop at A18 -- so the fault codes are the
published procedure for this board, and they are what the app presents.
Every fault code below records the verdict for BOTH branches, because knowing
that an in-tolerance reading indicts a different assembly is the whole value of
the code; a reading with no verdict just moves the question.

overview.summary: Two unrelated jobs on one board. The regulator section takes unregulated dc from the Filter/PA Supply assembly (A18) and produces thirteen regulated rails plus one unregulated fused rail for the analog assemblies. The guard crossing section is a self-contained inguard computer -- a Hitachi 637A01Y0 microcontroller with external RAM, EPROM, watchdog and reset supervision -- that drives the guarded digital bus and talks to the unguarded CPU (A20) over a fibre-optic serial link. It also generates the 8 MHz sine wave several analog assemblies need. The two sections share only the board and its supplies, so a fault is usually in one or the other, and the test point numbering follows that split: TP1-TP19 are regulator, TP51-TP65 are digital.
overview.connectors: P801 / P802, DIN 41612 type C, 64-pin right angle, mating with J801 / J802 on the Analog Motherboard (A3).

OSC.note: Fixed TO-220 regulators from the unregulated +15 OSCR / -15 OSCR. C2 and C5 stabilise U2 and U3; CR3 and CR5 block reverse voltage, CR2 and CR7 protect against input shorts. Used exclusively by the Oscillator Output (A12) and Oscillator Control (A13) assemblies.

LH.note: TO-3 regulators U11 (+5 RLH) and U8 (+5 LH) and TO-220 U12 (-5 LH). R13 with CR34/CR35 lifts U8 and U11 above their fixed +5 V, which is why +5 LH reads 5.1 V and +5 RLH reads 5.975 V rather than 5.0 V. +8 RLH is not regulated at all: it is the unregulated +5 LHR simply fused by F1.

S.note: S COM is the return for all six and is also connected to LH COM. The ±44 S pair are adjustable TO-39 regulators (U10, U13) fronted by emitter followers Q2 and Q1, which keep the regulator out of an excessive input-output differential during a short; PTC resistors R60 and R61 shunt 28 mA normally and limit to under 17 mA into a short. ±17 S are adjustable TO-3 regulators U6 and U7 set by R5/R6 and R10/R11. ±15 S are fixed TO-220 regulators U4 and U9 running off the ±17 SR inputs.

FR1.note: TO-39 regulator from the unregulated +30 FR1R, set by R1 and R2. FR1 COM is its own return, floating with respect to the other commons.

FR2.note: Identical circuit to FR1 with its own floating return: TO-39 regulator from +30 FR2R, set by R4 and R8.

DIGITAL.note: The inguard computer: microcontroller U56 (Hitachi 637A01Y0, 16 KB internal EPROM) with 8 KB external static RAM U62, EPROM U64, watchdog counters U59/U63, reset supervisor U60 and reset switch SW51. Y51 (4.9152 MHz) clocks the microcontroller; Y52 (8.000 MHz) with U51 generates the 8 MHz sine wave for the analog assemblies. U57 drives the fibre-optic link to the unguarded CPU (A20). The section runs from +5 LH through choke L51, so a dead digital section with a dead +5 LH is an LH fault, not a digital one.

faultCodes.title: +17 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +17 S supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Switch Matrix assembly (A8) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: -17 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the -17 S supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Switch Matrix assembly (A8) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: +15 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +15 S supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Output assembly (A13) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: -15 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the -15 S supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Output assembly (A13) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: +42 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +44 S supply reads out of tolerance. Check the unregulated +44 S on A18 first (COM = A18 TP22, HI = A18 TP7, +45 V to +75 V); if that is good, measure the regulated rail here.
faultCodes.verdict: Unregulated out of tolerance: A18 is faulty. Regulated out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. Both in tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Output assembly (A13) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: -42 S Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the -44 S supply reads out of tolerance. Check the unregulated -44 S on A18 first (COM = A18 TP22, HI = A18 TP9, -45 V to -75 V); if that is good, measure the regulated rail here.
faultCodes.verdict: Unregulated out of tolerance: A18 is faulty. Regulated out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. Both in tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Output assembly (A13) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: LH Com Ground Fault
faultCodes.measure: The Current/Hi-Res assembly (A7) connects LH COM to the SDL line, where the ADC on the DAC assembly measures it against RCOM
faultCodes.verdict: A shifted LH COM points at this assembly's LH return or the motherboard path to it; the measurement itself is made on A11, so a bad ADC reads the same way.

faultCodes.title: -5 LH Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the -5 LH supply reads out of tolerance. Check the unregulated -5 LH on A18 first (COM = A18 TP3, HI = A18 TP6, -8 V to -16 V); if that is good, measure the regulated rail here.
faultCodes.verdict: Unregulated out of tolerance: A18 is faulty. Regulated out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. Both in tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Switch Matrix assembly (A8) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: +5 RLH Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +5 RLH supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.expected: +4.9 V to +5.5 V as printed in §5-2 — but see the caveat: Table 2-10 and the sheet-1 annotation both give +5.55 V to +6.40 V
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Switch Matrix assembly (A8) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: +8 RLH Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +8 RLH supply reads out of tolerance
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance: replace fuse F1 on this assembly. In tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Switch Matrix assembly (A8) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: +15 OSC Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the +15 OSC supply reads outside +14.2 V to +15.8 V. Check the unregulated +15 OSC on A18 first (COM = A18 TP4, HI = A18 TP2, +19 V to +35 V); if that is good, measure the regulated rail here.
faultCodes.verdict: Unregulated out of tolerance: A18 is faulty. Regulated out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. Both in tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Control assembly (A12) is faulty.

faultCodes.title: -15 OSC Supply Fault
faultCodes.measure: Instrument dormant; the -15 OSC supply reads outside -14.2 V to -15.8 V. Check the unregulated -15 OSC on A18 first (COM = A18 TP4, HI = A18 TP5, -19 V to -35 V); if that is good, measure the regulated rail here.
faultCodes.verdict: Unregulated out of tolerance: A18 is faulty. Regulated out of tolerance: A17 is faulty. Both in tolerance: the diagnostic circuit on the Oscillator Control assembly (A12) is faulty. Note that §5-2 misprints the assembly as (A7) in this entry and repeats TP5 for both the A18 and A17 measurements; the A17 point is TP5 on this board.

faultCodes.title: OSC Com Ground Fault
faultCodes.measure: The Oscillator Control assembly (A12) connects OSC COM to the SDL line, where the ADC on the DAC assembly measures it against RCOM
faultCodes.verdict: A shifted OSC COM points at this assembly's OSC return or the motherboard path to it; the measurement is made on A11, so a bad ADC reads the same way.

faultCodes.title: S Com Ground Fault
faultCodes.measure: The Current/Hi-Res assembly (A7) connects S COM to the SDL line, where the ADC on the DAC assembly measures it against RCOM
faultCodes.verdict: A shifted S COM points at this assembly's S return or the motherboard path to it; the measurement is made on A11, so a bad ADC reads the same way.

componentNotes.U1: TO-39 regulator for +30 FR1. Output set by R1/R2.
componentNotes.U2: Fixed +15 V TO-220 regulator for +15 OSC.
componentNotes.U3: Fixed -15 V TO-220 regulator for -15 OSC.
componentNotes.U4: Fixed +15 V TO-220 regulator for +15 S, fed from the unregulated +17 SR.
componentNotes.U5: TO-39 regulator for +30 FR2. Output set by R4/R8.
componentNotes.U6: TO-3 low-dropout regulator for +17 S. Output set by R5/R6.
componentNotes.U7: TO-3 low-dropout regulator for -17 S. Output set by R10/R11.
componentNotes.U8: TO-3 +5 V regulator for +5 LH, lifted to 5.1 V by R13 with CR34/CR35.
componentNotes.U9: Fixed -15 V TO-220 regulator for -15 S, fed from the unregulated -17 SR.
componentNotes.U10: TO-39 adjustable regulator for +44 S. Output set by R14/R15; provides the current and thermal limiting.
componentNotes.U11: TO-3 +5 V regulator for +5 RLH, lifted to 5.975 V by R13 with CR34/CR35.
componentNotes.U12: Fixed -5 V TO-220 regulator for -5 LH.
componentNotes.U13: TO-39 adjustable regulator for -44 S. Output set by R17/R18.
componentNotes.U51: Hex inverter; with Y52 forms the 8 MHz oscillator whose output leaves at TP62.
componentNotes.U56: Hitachi 637A01Y0 microcontroller, the inguard CPU. 16 KB internal EPROM, 256 bytes internal RAM, clocked by Y51 at 4.9152 MHz.
componentNotes.U57: Open-collector AND driver for the fibre-optic transmit line (XMT, TP57).
componentNotes.U58: PAL address decoder for the inguard memory map.
componentNotes.U59: Watchdog counter. Its output reaches TP63 (POPIN).
componentNotes.U60: Voltage supervisor, 4.55 V sense. Drives RES* (TP60) with the watchdog.
componentNotes.U62: 8K x 8 static CMOS RAM, external RAM for the inguard CPU at A000-BFFF.
componentNotes.U64: EPROM in socket X3 on the 1996 board. The Rev 9 list and the photographed board carry Fluke 881698 (27C256) instead of 600137.
componentNotes.Q1: Emitter follower ahead of U13, protecting it from an excessive input-output differential during a -44 S short.
componentNotes.Q2: Emitter follower ahead of U10, doing the same job for +44 S.
componentNotes.F1: 3.15 A slow-blow. The only fuse on the board; it is what makes +8 RLH out of the unregulated +5 LHR, so an absent +8 RLH means check F1 before anything else.
componentNotes.R60: PTC thermistor shunting U10. Passes 28 mA normally and limits to under 17 mA at 25 °C into an output short.
componentNotes.R61: PTC thermistor shunting U13, the -44 S counterpart of R60.
componentNotes.Y51: 4.9152 MHz crystal for microcontroller U56. ECLK at TP61 is this divided by four.
componentNotes.Y52: 8.000 MHz crystal for the sine wave supplied to the analog assemblies, output at TP62.
componentNotes.L51: 3-turn choke feeding the guarded digital section from +5 LH.
componentNotes.T51: 8 MHz RF transformer coupling the sine wave off the board.
componentNotes.J801: Board connector, DIN 41612 type C 64-pin right angle. Silkscreened and drawn as P801; see the caveat on the designator conflict.
componentNotes.J802: Board connector, DIN 41612 type C 64-pin right angle. Silkscreened and drawn as P802; see the caveat on the designator conflict.

caveats.title: The board connectors are called J801/J802 in the parts list and P801/P802 everywhere else
caveats.text: Table 6-22 lists them as J801 and J802, while the component locator drawing, the schematic sheets and the board silkscreen all say P801 and P802. J801/J802 are also the names §2-19 gives the mating connectors on the Analog Motherboard (A3), so the parts list is naming this board's connectors after the sockets they plug into. A18's list does not do this — it names its own connectors P901/P902. The markers here are placed on the P801/P802 outlines; searching either name finds them.

caveats.title: Table 2-10 is missing the +15 S row
caveats.text: §2-71 says the regulator section has thirteen regulated outputs and one unregulated one, and §2-74 describes the +15 S regulator U4 in full, but Table 2-10 lists only twelve rows and +15 S is the one absent. Its expectation here comes from fault code 3602.

caveats.title: Table 2-10 loses the sign on the -15 S row
caveats.text: The signal name is printed '15S' with the nominal '-15V' beside it. The sheet 1 legend gives TP19 = -15S, and fault code 3603 expects -14.2 V to -15.8 V, so the rail is negative and the printed name is simply missing its minus sign.

caveats.title: The ±17 S nominals in Table 2-10 are the near limit, not the centre
caveats.text: Table 2-10 gives +17.000 V ±475 mV, which would be a band of +16.53 V to +17.48 V. The annotation on schematic sheet 1 says +17.0 V to +17.95 V and fault code 3600 says +17.0 V to +18.0 V — the same width, shifted half a volt up. -17 S behaves the same way: table -17.000 V ±835 mV against sheet and fault code -17.03 V to -18.7 V. Two independent sources agreeing against the table is the reason the band shown here is theirs.

caveats.title: Fault code 3608 disagrees with Table 2-10 about +5 RLH
caveats.text: §5-2 expects +4.9 V to +5.5 V at TP14. Table 2-10 gives +5.975 V ±425 mV and schematic sheet 1 annotates +5.55 V to +6.40 V — the two bands do not overlap at all. §2-73 explains why the rail is high: R13 with CR34/CR35 lifts U11 above its fixed +5 V. The expectation shown here follows the two agreeing sources, so a board reading 5.9 V is good even though 3608 would call it a failure.

caveats.title: A17 has no numbered troubleshooting section
caveats.text: Chapter 5's component-level procedures run from 5-4 (A5) to 5-23 (A18) and never reach A17. The published procedure for this board is the 3600-series fault codes in §5-2, which is what the Fault codes panel lists.

caveats.title: Six parts changed between the 1996 and Rev 9 parts lists
caveats.text: CR35, MP38, R19, U58, U64 and Y51 have different Fluke stock numbers in the two revisions (Y51's 4.9152 MHz crystal is 800367 in 1996 and 800357 in Rev 9), and Rev 9 adds MP23 (a guard-crossing shield) and MP24–MP27 (pop rivets) that the 1996 list does not have. Rev 9 also drops the 28-pin socket X3. The photographed board carries the Rev 9 EPROM (881698), so it is a Rev 9-era assembly. Both descriptions are kept: the info card shows the 1996 entry with the Rev 9 one beside it as 'as built'.
